- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid missing early reversal.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply downward correction starting from day 10–14 of forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates late-period (days 20–30) prices; apply 1–2% downward correction for final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “negative” sentiment, model tends to ignore it; add 0.1–0.3 to forecast if sentiment is consistently low or negative.
